name: Pierfrancesco Maran, Mélissa Camara - Accord provisoire - Am 6
title: REPORT on the proposal for a decision of the European Parliament and of the Council empowering France to accede to the Inter-American Convention for the Protection and Conservation of Sea Turtles
part_text: AMENDMENTS BY THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT\* to the Commission proposal DECISION (EU) 2026/…. OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of … empowering France to accede to the Inter-American Convention for the Protection and Conservation of Sea Turtles THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND THE COUNCIL OF THE EUROPEAN UNION, Having regard to the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, and in particular Article 43(2) thereof, Having regard to the proposal from the European Commission, Having regard to the opinion of the European Economic and Social Committee, Acting in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure, Whereas: (1) On 4 February 2025, France requested an empowerment from the Union to accede to the Inter-American Convention for the Protection and Conservation of Sea Turtles, done at Caracas on 1 December 1996 (the ‘Convention’), in order to strengthen its cooperation with the countries bordering its territories on the American continents in the area of the protection of marine turtle species occurring in seas adjacent to the American continents and the Caribbean. (2) Certain matters covered by the Convention fall within the Union's exclusive competence. In order to accede to the Convention, therefore, France is required to be empowered by the Union pursuant to Article 2(1) of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) for matters falling under the Union's exclusive competence. This Decision does not constitute an exercise of external competence by the Union as regards matters covered by the Convention that do not relate to an exclusive competence. (3) The Convention is in line with the Union’s policies in the fields of the protection of marine biological resources and the environment, in particular as regards measures for the protection and conservation of sea turtles. Since the Convention is open for accession to States on the American continents and in the Caribbean ▌, it is appropriate for the Union to empower France to accede to it. (4) French overseas countries and territories listed in Annex II to the TFEU, and their waters, are outside the territorial scope of the Treaties as regards, inter alia, the matters covered by the Convention for which the Union has exclusive competence. Therefore, this Decision is without prejudice to any rights or obligations of France that arise from the accession to the Convention in respect of those countries and territories, and their waters.
